text:
alex: FYI — canary 'canary-213' (2% traffic) started at 13:10 UTC and p95 token latency jumped ~2x vs baseline. I'm going to roll it back. Who wants the fast revert vs safe-disable?

maria: link to the perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rollouts/canary-213 :eyes:

suresh: +1 rollback. For fast revert we can call the rollout API to set traffic_split for that variant to 0. Example:

```
# quick revert (immediate)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/rollouts/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"rollout_id":"canary-213","traffic": {"canary-213": 0, "stable": 100}}'
```

jamie: Before nuking traffic, we should think about KV/prefix caches. Canary served a slightly different KV-keying (prefix v2) so disabling it abruptly may leave stale cache entries or partial K/V state. Two options: fast revert (good for availability) or safe-disable (drain + preserve cache).

emily: oncall here — I can watch infra metrics and error budget while you do it. Which command will you run?

alex: I'm leaning fast revert now because customer impact risk > minor cache staleness. Will run quick revert and then do a targeted cache sweep for canary keys.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout patch job queued (id: rj-1764204822). Will apply traffic update in ~5s.

ops-oncall: If you do immediate traffic flip, plan to invalidate canary prefixes after traffic is 0. We have a cache purge endpoint: `/admin/cache/purge` — use `prefix=canary-213:`. Example:

```
# purge only canary keys
curl -X POST https://infra.redwood.ai/admin/cache/purge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefix":"canary-213:","confirm":true}'
```

maria: remember to bump the throttle/quota guards back if you had any overrides for canary. We temporarily gave canary a higher token quota for perf testing. See: `/internal/quotas/canary-213`

suresh: Also flip the feature flag so new traffic won't re-enable the alternate keying:

```
# feature flag disable
redwood-ffctl set --key rollout.canary-213.keying_version --value v1
```

jamie: Proposed safe-disable pattern for future rollouts (if we want less churn):
- Step 1: set traffic_split canary -> 0 (fast revert)
- Step 2: set canary to "drain" so instances stop accepting new prefix writes but continue serving existing cached responses for T_drain window
- Step 3: after drain window, purge canary prefixes and revert keying flag
- Step 4: monitor regressions for 30m, then delete canary allocations

This avoids losing hot KV entries immediately and reduces cold-start cost if we re-roll. We should add this to the runbook.

emily: doing the fast revert now. Notifying SRE paging to watch NLB latencies and token queue length.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout patch job started (rj-1764204822) -> applying traffic delta.

alex: ran the curl patch above, got 200. Traffic now at 0 for canary-213.

ops-oncall: I'm running the cache purge for prefix `canary-213:` now. ETA ~12s.

ops-oncall: cache purge complete. Purged ~8.6k keys.

maria: I reverted the quota overrides and reset canary rate_limit to baseline.

jamie: flip the FF back to v1 confirmed?

suresh: flag set back to v1 and propagated to edge config (checked).

emily: watching dashboards — error rate stable, p95 returned to baseline. No alerts firing. :tada:

alex: thanks everyone. I'll update the rollout entry and add a short note to the runbook about drain window and cache-sweep ordering. Follow-up: create an automation to (a) set traffic->0, (b) schedule cache purge 30s after traffic=0, (c) flip FF flag. Could be a single atomic rollback playbook.

maria: +1 for automation. Also add a telemetry check that confirms prefix naming/version parity before canary promotion.

jamie: opening a quick follow-up PR for runbook edits and the automation ticket.

alex: ok closing thread — will file postmortem if we see recurrence. Thanks all.
